module.purpose: Provides Content Security Policy nonce generation, request propagation, and response-header emission for web page requests.
module.summary: This module implements CSP handling across Node and Next.js request/response interfaces. It recognizes existing nonces, filters requests to page paths, generates cryptographic nonces when policy enforcement is enabled, stores them on requests, and conditionally emits a normalized CSP header on responses.
module.businessContext: Supports browser security for the web application by restricting executable and loadable resources. Failure can prevent page rendering or weaken protection against injected scripts and unauthorized resource loading.
functions: getCspPolicy (~L9-38): Builds a nonce-aware Content Security Policy string.

safeParseString (~L48-53): Validates unknown values before treating them as strings.
csp (~L55-111): Generates, propagates, and emits CSP nonces for requests.

env: Reads process.env.CSP_POLICY to determine whether CSP processing is enabled and whether non-strict styles are allowed.
mutationOfArg: Mutates the request x-nonce header when a page request requires CSP.
Mutates the response headers by setting Content-Security-Policy when enforcement is requested.

assumptions.description: The runtime provides process.env.CSP_POLICY and its presence enables CSP processing for eligible page requests.
Callers provide request objects compatible with either Node headers or the Next.js cache/header API.
The runtime provides crypto.getRandomValues and URL parsing support.

concurrencyModel.notes: All operations are synchronous; nonce generation uses per-call cryptographic randomness and request/response mutation is local to the supplied objects.

moduleContractTests.scenario: A null request is passed to the CSP middleware.
The request already contains a string x-nonce header.
moduleContractTests.rationale: Existing nonce propagation avoids generating a replacement nonce.

moduleContractTests.scenario: The request contains an existing x-nonce value that is not a string.
moduleContractTests.rationale: The middleware preserves the safe-parse failure contract for malformed nonce values.

moduleContractTests.scenario: A request without a URL is provided and has no existing nonce.
CSP is enabled but the request targets an API or Next.js internal path.
moduleContractTests.rationale: CSP nonce generation is restricted to page-path requests.

moduleContractTests.scenario: An eligible page request has CSP enabled and enforcement requested.
moduleContractTests.then: res.headers["Content-Security-Policy"] is a non-empty normalized policy containing the generated nonce
moduleContractTests.rationale: Pins the response security-header contract and nonce-policy coupling.

moduleContractTests.scenario: An eligible page request has CSP enabled and no existing nonce.
moduleContractTests.rationale: Downstream server rendering relies on the nonce being written to the request.

moduleContractTests.scenario: An eligible page request has CSP enabled but enforcement is not requested.
moduleContractTests.rationale: The implementation intentionally does not emit report-only or unenforced CSP headers.
